claims.text: The longest side of a right-angled triangle, opposite the right angle, is called the hypotenuse.
Adjacent, tangent and median are not names for the longest side of a right-angled triangle.
Pythagoras' theorem states that the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
Babylonian scribes were using this relationship by about 1800 BC, more than 1,000 years before Pythagoras was born.
